records.description: Neurovascular Coupling denotes the admissible process-level arising through which local neural activity is translated into matched changes of blood supply within the neurovascular unit. Activity-associated signals, among them extracellular potassium sensed by capillary endothelial inward-rectifier (Kir2.1) channels whose availability depends on membrane PIP2, initiate endothelial hyperpolarization that is conducted upstream through gap-junction-coupled endothelium to dilate feeding arterioles and increase red-cell flux; mural cells, astrocytes and neuromodulators contribute further routes whose relative roles remain open. The arising couples two organizational systems, neural activity as the initiating signal and the vascular network as substrate and effector, and is not a property of either alone. Within SOMA this arising is classified as a process because its identity lies in ordered sensing, conduction and vasomotor response through time rather than in a vessel object or a static perfusion pattern.
records.name: Neurovascular Coupling
records.shortDescription: Process-level coupling of local cerebral blood flow to neural activity, in which activity-associated signals are sensed by the vascular wall and conducted to upstream arterioles to raise local perfusion.
records.summary: Process-level coupling of local cerebral blood flow to neural activity, in which activity-associated signals are sensed by the vascular wall and conducted to upstream arterioles to raise local perfusion.

records.description: Restricted Adult Neurogenesis denotes the admissible process-level arising through which adult neural stem cells in restricted niches, principally the dentate subgranular zone and the subventricular zone with its migratory route to the olfactory bulb, leave quiescence, proliferate, commit to neuronal fate, migrate, mature and integrate as functional circuit members. Niche signals and local circuit activity, such as parvalbumin-interneuron GABA acting on radial glia-like stem cells, regulate quiescence and fate; experience such as learning and running modulates proliferation and survival; integrated adult-born neurons receive input, form output synapses and can change network-level discrimination. The process is restricted: it is absent from most of the adult brain, declines with age, and its extent in adult humans remains contested. It adds new neurons and does not concern the rewiring of existing ones. Within SOMA this arising is classified as a process because its identity lies in an ordered developmental trajectory of new cells through time.
records.name: Restricted Adult Neurogenesis
records.shortDescription: Process-level generation, maturation and functional integration of new neurons from adult neural stem cells in restricted niches, at rates that differ strongly between species and decline with age.
records.summary: Process-level generation, maturation and functional integration of new neurons from adult neural stem cells in restricted niches, at rates that differ strongly between species and decline with age.

records.description: Working Memory and Executive Functions denotes the admissible process-level organization by which neural systems temporarily sustain, manipulate, update, and control activity patterns over short temporal windows while exerting top-down regulation over processing and action selection. Within Level 6 this arising consists in temporally extended operations of transient maintenance, gating, inhibition, monitoring, switching, selective biasing, and controlled updating across distributed neural circuits. Within SOMA this arising is classified as a process because its identity is defined by ordered control dynamics unfolding through time rather than by one bounded object, static pattern, or regime property alone. Working memory at this level is treated as an operational control process of neural dynamics rather than as long-term storage, narrative identity, or symbolic reasoning. This arising establishes the short-horizon control architecture through which neural systems maintain task-relevant states, regulate interference, coordinate flexible resource allocation, and support context-sensitive selection under changing demands.
records.name: Working Memory and Executive Functions
records.shortDescription: Process-level temporary maintenance, manipulation, and top-down control of neural activity enabling short-window retention and flexible regulation.
records.summary: Process-level temporary maintenance, manipulation, and top-down control of neural activity enabling short-window retention and flexible regulation.

records.description: Neural Mechanisms of Symbolic Representation denote the hypothesized admissible property-level arising through which neural organization acquires the capacity to form, stabilize, manipulate, and recombine internal representational states that functionally stand in for classes of objects, relations, actions, rules, or hypothetical configurations beyond immediate sensory instantiation. This arising is not identical to simple sensory coding, stimulus-response association, or transient activation of perceptual traces. It refers to a higher-order representational capacity in which internally maintained neural states can preserve abstract reference, support combinatorial transformation, participate in rule-sensitive manipulation, and remain operative across delays, context shifts, and non-present targets. The property depends on coordinated cognitive control, working-memory maintenance, ensemble specialization, and recurrent representational stabilization, through which neural systems can detach operative structure from immediate perceptual input and use it in planning, inference, communication, and structured reasoning. Within SOMA this is a property because it characterizes an organized neural system by a stable representational capacity rather than by one isolated process episode, bounded object, or single pattern instance.
records.name: Neural Mechanisms of Symbolic Representation
records.shortDescription: Property-level neural capacity to sustain and manipulate abstract internal representations detached from immediate sensory instantiation.
records.summary: Property-level neural capacity to sustain and manipulate abstract internal representations detached from immediate sensory instantiation.

records.description: Brain Oscillations and Rhythms denotes the admissible pattern-level formation of coherent temporal organization across distributed neural populations, expressed through recurring frequency bands, phase relations, synchrony structures, and cross-frequency coupling regimes. Within Level 6 this arising is not a single event of firing and not an individuated object, but a reproducible dynamical pattern distributed across many interacting neural carriers and recurrent pathways. Within SOMA this arising is classified as a pattern because its identity is determined by stable relational organization in time across neural ensembles rather than by one bounded material unit or by a single transition episode. These oscillatory regimes establish temporal windows for coordination, gating, routing, entrainment, and phase-sensitive interaction within and between neural networks. They function as network-level timing architectures that constrain when interactions become effective and how activity propagates, without yet implying semantic content, symbolic representation, cognition, or conscious experience as distinct higher-order arisings.
records.name: Brain Oscillations and Rhythms
records.shortDescription: Pattern-level coherent temporal organization of distributed neural activity expressed through recurrent frequencies, phase relations, and cross-network rhythmic coupling.
records.summary: Pattern-level coherent temporal organization of distributed neural activity expressed through recurrent frequencies, phase relations, and cross-network rhythmic coupling.

records.description: Neural Mechanisms of Social Recognition and Empathy denote the admissible process-level arising through which neural systems identify other agents, differentiate self-related from other-related signals, attribute socially relevant states, and generate affective or motivational resonance in response to the perceived condition of others. This arising is not a single emotion and not one fixed social module. It consists in a temporally extended organization of agent detection, self–other discrimination, socially relevant perception, affective appraisal, state attribution, and resonance-sensitive response shaping across distributed neural circuits. Through this process, the nervous system can detect socially salient cues, map them onto internal evaluative and affective systems, and generate responses that support recognition, concern, alignment, avoidance, helping, or other socially mediated behavior. The arising therefore captures the neural process architecture underlying social recognition and empathy as an organized cross-domain coupling of perception, affect, memory, valuation, and control rather than as a purely symbolic or purely emotional event.
records.name: Neural Mechanisms of Social Recognition and Empathy
records.shortDescription: Process-level neural differentiation of other agents and resonant coupling to their perceived states through social recognition and affective alignment.
records.summary: Process-level neural differentiation of other agents and resonant coupling to their perceived states through social recognition and affective alignment.

records.description: Placebo Responses and Psychosomatic Modulation denote the admissible process-level arising through which expectation, learning history, contextual framing, affective valuation, and higher-order neural state organization induce reliable changes in physiological regulation, immune activity, pain processing, autonomic output, and symptom expression. This arising is not reducible to conscious belief alone and not limited to one clinical setting. It consists in a temporally extended downward modulation by which neural representations of context, treatment meaning, anticipated outcome, and bodily significance are translated through autonomic, neuroendocrine, immune, and neuromodulatory pathways into measurable shifts in organism-level function. The process can amplify recovery-enabling responses, suppress symptoms, alter pain sensitivity, or reshape physiological set-points without introducing a new external pharmacological cause. Within SOMA this is a process because its identity lies in ordered cross-level transformation from neural-state configuration into bodily regulatory change rather than in a static property or bounded anatomical object.
records.name: Placebo Responses and Psychosomatic Modulation
records.shortDescription: Process-level downward modulation in which expectation, learning, context, and affective neural states reshape physiological regulation, immune activity, pain, and symptom expression.
records.summary: Process-level downward modulation in which expectation, learning, context, and affective neural states reshape physiological regulation, immune activity, pain, and symptom expression.

records.description: Thalamic Visual Relay and Gain Control denotes the admissible process-level regulation by which thalamic nuclei integrate retinal input with cortical feedback and neuromodulatory influences to control transmission, amplification, filtering, and temporal precision of visual signals. Within Level 6 this arising consists in temporally extended gating operations that determine which visual inputs are propagated, suppressed, synchronized, or amplified before cortical integration. Within SOMA this arising is classified as a process because its identity is defined by ongoing context-sensitive regulation of signal flow through time rather than by one static thalamic structure, bounded object, or stable property alone. This arising formalizes the thalamus as an active regulator of sensory throughput rather than a passive relay, implementing gain control, noise suppression, phase-sensitive transmission, and conditional routing aligned with attentional state, arousal, and broader neural regime conditions. It establishes the process architecture through which early visual input becomes selectively admitted into larger cortical processing dynamics.
records.name: Thalamic Visual Relay and Gain Control
records.shortDescription: Process-level regulated thalamic routing and modulation of visual signals between retinal input and cortical processing networks.
records.summary: Process-level regulated thalamic routing and modulation of visual signals between retinal input and cortical processing networks.

records.description: Primary Visual Cortex Feature Maps denotes the admissible pattern-level organization in which thalamocortical input and intracortical coupling give rise to stable, spatially ordered neural selectivity for elementary visual features. Within Level 6 this arising is not a single processing event and not one bounded cortical object, but a reproducible relational pattern distributed across cortical tissue through topographic, columnar, and feature-selective organization. Within SOMA this arising is classified as a pattern because its identity is determined by ordered spatial arrangement of selectivity relations across many neural carriers rather than by one isolated process or one intrinsic property considered alone. These maps encode orientation, edge structure, spatial frequency, ocular dominance, motion-related components, and retinotopic correspondence through structured cortical layouts that constrain later visual processing. This arising marks the transition from modality-specific sensory inflow to organized feature-representational architecture, establishing a canonical cortical basis for downstream visual form analysis.
records.name: Primary Visual Cortex Feature Maps
records.shortDescription: Pattern-level cortical organization of stable feature-selective maps for orientation, edges, spatial frequency, and related visual primitives.
records.summary: Pattern-level cortical organization of stable feature-selective maps for orientation, edges, spatial frequency, and related visual primitives.

records.description: Predictive and Top-Down Attentional Modulation of Visual Processing denote the admissible process-level arising through which higher-order neural states influence visual processing by generating context-sensitive expectations, biasing gain allocation, shaping error sensitivity, and selectively enhancing behaviorally relevant information across recurrent visual pathways. This arising is not tied to one narrow formal doctrine alone, but captures the broader family of top-down predictive and expectation-sensitive control processes through which incoming sensory signals are compared with internally maintained context, task demands, prior structure, and current behavioral goals. The process unfolds through iterative feedback-dependent modulation of thalamocortical and corticocortical pathways, altering which visual inputs are amplified, suppressed, routed, stabilized, or prioritized for further processing. The arising therefore formalizes a recurrent visual-control regime in which perception is shaped not only by feedforward sensory drive but also by internally organized expectations, attentional weighting, and dynamic contextual selection.
records.name: Predictive and Top-Down Attentional Modulation of Visual Processing
records.shortDescription: Process-level downward modulation of visual processing through expectation-sensitive feedback, error weighting, and context-dependent attentional gain control.
records.summary: Process-level downward modulation of visual processing through expectation-sensitive feedback, error weighting, and context-dependent attentional gain control.

records.description: Structural Remodeling of Mature Neural Circuits denotes the admissible process-level arising through which already established circuits revise which synaptic contacts exist. Dendritic spines and their synapses form and are eliminated at a baseline rate; learning a new motor skill transiently increases formation and elimination, and a learning-specific subset of new spines is stabilized for months, while retraining on a familiar task does not raise turnover. After focal cortical stroke, peri-infarct tissue shows weeks of elevated spine formation together with vascular remodeling. The arising changes connectivity itself rather than the efficacy of existing synapses, and it adds no neurons. Within SOMA this arising is classified as a process because its identity lies in ordered turnover and selective retention of structural elements through time.
records.name: Structural Remodeling of Mature Neural Circuits
records.shortDescription: Process-level formation, elimination and selective long-term stabilization of synaptic contacts in mature circuits, increased by learning and after injury, without birth of new neurons.
records.summary: Process-level formation, elimination and selective long-term stabilization of synaptic contacts in mature circuits, increased by learning and after injury, without birth of new neurons.

records.description: Microglial Regulation of Neural Circuits denotes the admissible process-level arising through which microglia, resident brain cells of myeloid immune lineage, continuously sample the parenchyma with motile processes and converge on injured sites, engulf less active synaptic inputs through complement C3 and its receptor CR3 during circuit refinement, and, in the proposed purinergic feedback, sense neuronal ATP through P2RY12 and generate adenosine via CD39 and CD73 that suppresses neuronal activity through A1 receptors. The arising couples innate-immune machinery to neural network structure and excitability: it refines developing connectivity and limits excessive synchrony and seizure susceptibility, while its protective immune functions remain partly hypothetical. Within SOMA this arising is classified as a process because its identity lies in ongoing surveillance, engulfment and feedback dynamics rather than in a static property of glial tissue.
records.name: Microglial Regulation of Neural Circuits
records.shortDescription: Process-level regulation of neural circuits by brain-resident immune cells through continuous process surveillance, activity- and complement-dependent engulfment of synaptic inputs, and purinergic negative feedback on neuronal activity.
records.summary: Process-level regulation of neural circuits by brain-resident immune cells through continuous process surveillance, activity- and complement-dependent engulfment of synaptic inputs, and purinergic negative feedback on neuronal activity.

records.description: Activity-Dependent Myelination and Conduction Tuning denotes the admissible process-level arising through which neural activity and sensory experience regulate oligodendrocyte generation and the geometry of myelin internodes on active axons, thereby changing conduction velocity and the timing of signal arrival. In the developing optic nerve, visual deprivation shortens internodes formed during deprivation, increases mature oligodendrocyte counts and slows compound action potential conduction, while measured myelin thickness and refractory recovery are unchanged. This plasticity acts on axonal transmission timing rather than on synaptic efficacy. Within SOMA this arising is classified as a process because its identity lies in an ordered, experience-dependent remodeling of myelinated conduction through time.
records.name: Activity-Dependent Myelination and Conduction Tuning
records.shortDescription: Process-level adjustment of oligodendrocyte number, internode length and axonal conduction velocity by neural activity and sensory experience.
records.summary: Process-level adjustment of oligodendrocyte number, internode length and axonal conduction velocity by neural activity and sensory experience.

records.description: Cognitive Processing and Decision Making denotes the admissible process-level organization by which neural systems integrate distributed activity over time, evaluate competing alternatives, and commit to selected internal states or action-guiding outcomes through coordinated population dynamics. Within Level 6 this arising consists in temporally extended operations such as evidence accumulation, state competition, inhibitory selection, threshold crossing, and commitment formation across interacting neural assemblies. Within SOMA this arising is classified as a process because its identity is defined by ordered transitions and regulated selection dynamics unfolding through time rather than by a static pattern, bounded object, or abstract property considered alone. Cognition at this level therefore refers to structured neural control and admissible state selection implemented within network dynamics, without yet requiring symbolic language, explicit social norm systems, or reflective self-awareness. This arising establishes the process architecture by which neural systems transform distributed signals into constrained selections that guide behavior, internal regulation, and context-sensitive control.
records.name: Cognitive Processing and Decision Making
records.shortDescription: Process-level integration, evaluation, and selection among alternative neural states producing controlled commitment to internal or action-guiding outcomes.
records.summary: Process-level integration, evaluation, and selection among alternative neural states producing controlled commitment to internal or action-guiding outcomes.

records.description: Sensory Integration and Perception denotes the admissible process-level organization by which neural systems combine signals from multiple sensory modalities into unified, spatially and temporally coherent perceptual states. Within Level 6 this arising consists in temporally extended operations of convergence, alignment, weighting, disambiguation, contextual modulation, and stability maintenance across distributed neural pathways receiving heterogeneous sensory inputs. Within SOMA this arising is classified as a process because its identity is defined by ordered integrative transformations unfolding through time rather than by a static object, isolated pattern, or abstract property. Perception at this level therefore refers to the regulated neural construction of integrated sensory states that remain sufficiently coherent under noise, incompleteness, and cross-modal variation, without yet presupposing conscious awareness, semantic interpretation, or symbolic categorization. This arising establishes the process architecture through which sensory systems transform parallel modality-specific inputs into coordinated perceptual outcomes that can guide later cognition and action.
records.name: Sensory Integration and Perception
records.shortDescription: Process-level integration, alignment, and stabilization of multisensory neural inputs into coherent perceptual states under noise and partial information.
records.summary: Process-level integration, alignment, and stabilization of multisensory neural inputs into coherent perceptual states under noise and partial information.

records.description: Motor Coordination and Control denotes the admissible process-level organization by which neural systems integrate sensory input, internal state, and motor command dynamics to generate coherent, adaptive movement patterns. Within Level 6 this arising consists in temporally extended operations of sequencing, initiation, timing regulation, predictive adjustment, feedback correction, gain control, and distributed stabilization across sensorimotor circuits. Within SOMA this arising is classified as a process because its identity is defined by ordered control dynamics unfolding through time rather than by a static network pattern, bounded object, or isolated property. Motor control at this level therefore refers to the structured neural regulation of movement execution and online correction within distributed circuits, without yet requiring explicit intentionality, goal semantics, or social-context interpretation. This arising establishes the process architecture through which neural systems transform integrated signals into coordinated motor outputs that remain stable, adaptable, and error-sensitive under changing conditions.
records.name: Motor Coordination and Control
records.shortDescription: Process-level neural regulation of movement through sequencing, timing, prediction, and feedback-based stabilization of motor execution.
records.summary: Process-level neural regulation of movement through sequencing, timing, prediction, and feedback-based stabilization of motor execution.

records.description: Emotional and Affective Processing denotes the admissible property-level emergence of global evaluative state organization within neural systems, expressed through distributed valence, arousal, salience, and motivational biasing conditions that modulate ongoing processing across multiple circuits. Within Level 6 this arising is not a single bounded object and not merely a transient sequence of events, but a system-wide property of neural organization in which large-scale processing becomes selectively biased toward particular priorities, thresholds, and response tendencies. Within SOMA this arising is classified as a property because its identity lies in a regime-like evaluative condition attributable to the organized neural system rather than in one isolated process or pattern alone. Affect at this level functions as a dynamic evaluative property that reallocates processing resources, shifts learning sensitivity, alters decision thresholds, modulates perceptual weighting, and changes motor readiness across distributed networks, without yet requiring symbolic interpretation, language, or socially constructed meaning. This arising establishes the evaluative bias architecture through which neural systems become differentially tuned to relevance, urgency, and adaptive priority.
records.name: Emotional and Affective Processing
records.shortDescription: Property-level global evaluative state organization in neural systems that biases cognition, perception, learning, and action through distributed modulation.
records.summary: Property-level global evaluative state organization in neural systems that biases cognition, perception, learning, and action through distributed modulation.

records.description: Global Neurotransmitter Modulation denotes the admissible property-level organization by which diffuse neuromodulatory transmitter systems impose system-wide chemical biasing conditions across large-scale neural networks. Within Level 6 this arising is expressed through broad modulation of excitability, gain, responsiveness, learning sensitivity, threshold setting, and regime selection by transmitters such as dopamine, serotonin, noradrenaline, and acetylcholine acting over extended spatial and temporal scales. Within SOMA this arising is classified as a property because its identity lies in a global regulatory condition attributable to the organized neural system rather than in one isolated event, bounded object, or static connectivity pattern. This arising configures whole-system operating modes that bias how existing networks process signals, respond to perturbation, and transition between functional regimes without requiring alteration of core network topology. It establishes a chemically mediated global control property through which neural systems become tunably reconfigurable across attention, arousal, reinforcement sensitivity, and state-dependent responsiveness.
records.name: Global Neurotransmitter Modulation
records.shortDescription: Property-level system-wide neuromodulatory state organization that shifts excitability, gain, learning sensitivity, and operating regimes across large-scale neural networks.
records.summary: Property-level system-wide neuromodulatory state organization that shifts excitability, gain, learning sensitivity, and operating regimes across large-scale neural networks.

records.description: Neuronal Avalanches and Near-Critical Network Dynamics denotes the admissible pattern-level organization in which collective neural activity propagates in cascades whose sizes and durations follow scale-spanning distributions, a regime shifted by changes of the excitation–inhibition balance and proposed to reflect operation near a critical transition. Within Level 6 this arising is not a single event and not a property of one neuron, but a reproducible relational pattern of collective dynamics across many neural carriers. Avalanche statistics alone do not establish criticality, which remains a hypothesis, and rhythmic phase synchronization is a distinct oscillatory pattern. Within SOMA this arising is classified as a pattern because its identity lies in the statistical organization of activity propagation rather than in one bounded object or process episode.
records.name: Neuronal Avalanches and Near-Critical Network Dynamics
records.shortDescription: Pattern-level scale-spanning cascade organization of collective neural activity (neuronal avalanches) and the near-critical operating regime it may indicate.
records.summary: Pattern-level scale-spanning cascade organization of collective neural activity (neuronal avalanches) and the near-critical operating regime it may indicate.

records.description: Emergence of Conscious Experience denotes the hypothesized admissible property-level arising through which distributed neural organization sustains an organized form of conscious access and experiential presence under conditions of sufficient large-scale integration, temporal coherence, recurrent availability, and cross-domain coordination. This arising is not identified with any single oscillation band, local circuit, anatomical structure, or one universally accepted mechanism. Instead, it refers to a regime-level property attributable to the organized neural system when neural dynamics become capable of enabling reportable, integrated, and temporally sustained experience as such. The node is therefore intentionally formulated at the level of admissibility rather than at the level of final explanatory closure. Within SOMA this is a property because its identity lies in a system-level condition of the organized neural whole, not in one bounded object, one isolated process episode, or one fixed connectivity pattern.
records.name: Emergence of Conscious Experience
records.shortDescription: Property-level organized experiential presence arising when neural organization sustains sufficiently integrated and temporally coherent conscious access.
records.summary: Property-level organized experiential presence arising when neural organization sustains sufficiently integrated and temporally coherent conscious access.

records.description: Social Organization of Animals denotes the admissible pattern-level stabilization of persistent group structures formed through sustained and structured interaction among multiple animals. Within Level 7 this arising is not a single event of coordination and not an individuated object, but a reproducible relational pattern distributed across interacting organisms through recurring association, dominance structure, cooperative allocation, synchronized movement, signaling regularities, and role differentiation. Within SOMA this arising is classified as a pattern because its identity is determined by stable organization of relations among multiple animal carriers rather than by one bounded body, isolated process episode, or single intrinsic property. This arising marks a transition from individual behavioral control to a group-level causal regime in which interaction topology constrains individual action and generates collective properties such as cohesion, hierarchy, division of roles, adaptive responsiveness, and distributed regulation. It persists despite partial turnover of individuals and operates through distributed constraint rather than centralized control.
records.name: Social Organization of Animals
records.shortDescription: Pattern-level stabilization of persistent group structures through coordinated inter-animal interaction, producing reproducible collective organization beyond individual behavior.
records.summary: Pattern-level stabilization of persistent group structures through coordinated inter-animal interaction, producing reproducible collective organization beyond individual behavior.

records.description: Social Roles and Stratification denotes the admissible pattern-level stabilization of differentiated positions within already organized animal groups, where recurrent interaction regularities consolidate into durable role-defined relations. Within Level 7 this arising is not a single dominance event and not an individuated object, but a reproducible relational pattern in which individuals cease to be functionally interchangeable and become associated with persistent expectations such as leadership, subordination, guarding, mediation, specialization, or preferential access. Within SOMA this arising is classified as a pattern because its identity is determined by stable organization of positional relations among multiple animal carriers rather than by one isolated process, bounded body, or intrinsic property. This arising introduces durable asymmetries in authority, access, influence, obligation, and responsibility, establishing a structured social geometry that constrains interaction pathways, regulates conflict and cooperation, and channels collective dynamics beyond the persistence of any particular individual occupant.
records.name: Social Roles and Stratification
records.shortDescription: Pattern-level stabilization of differentiated social positions, hierarchical asymmetries, and persistent role-defined relations within animal groups.
records.summary: Pattern-level stabilization of differentiated social positions, hierarchical asymmetries, and persistent role-defined relations within animal groups.

records.description: Political and Governance Structures denotes the admissible object-level formation of durable institutional configurations through which large-scale social systems define, enforce, and revise binding decisions across heterogeneous populations. Within Level 7 this arising is treated as an object because it consists in identifiable organized social formations composed of offices, roles, procedures, decision channels, legitimacy structures, and enforcement capacities that persist as bounded institutional units across episodes of participation and personnel turnover. Within SOMA this arising is not merely a transient governance process or a diffuse social property, but a persistent organized configuration through which authority becomes structurally embodied and socially operative. These structures formalize collective decision-making, codify legitimacy and compliance expectations, establish enforceable jurisdiction, and enable long-horizon coordination under scale, conflict, and complexity. They constrain behavior, regulate disputes, stabilize rule application, and maintain collective order beyond informal norms or voluntary exchange alone.
records.name: Political and Governance Structures
records.shortDescription: Object-level institutional configurations organizing collective rule-setting, authority, legitimacy, and enforcement across large-scale populations.
records.summary: Object-level institutional configurations organizing collective rule-setting, authority, legitimacy, and enforcement across large-scale populations.

records.description: Evolution of Complex Social Institutions denotes the admissible object-level formation of historically extended institutional systems through which governance structures, social norms, and recurrent practices consolidate into formally defined and reproductively persistent social objects. Within Level 7 this arising is treated as an object because institutions such as law, education, religion, science, and finance exist as identifiable organized formations with bounded rule systems, role hierarchies, enforcement channels, reproduction procedures, and reform pathways that persist across episodes of participation and across generations. Within SOMA this arising is not merely a governance process or a diffuse social property, but a durable institutional configuration capable of cumulative modification, path dependence, inertia, and selective adaptation under changing historical conditions. These institutions exert downward constraints on both individual and collective behavior while remaining sensitive to long-term environmental, economic, political, and cultural pressures. This arising marks a threshold at which social structures become historically extended objects with internal continuity and autonomous causal efficacy.
records.name: Evolution of Complex Social Institutions
records.shortDescription: Object-level historically extended institutional formations that reproduce, stabilize, and transform large-scale social coordination across generations.
records.summary: Object-level historically extended institutional formations that reproduce, stabilize, and transform large-scale social coordination across generations.

records.description: Cultural and Linguistic Evolutionary Change denotes the admissible process-level transformation through which symbolic systems, linguistic structures, shared practices, meanings, and transmissible cultural forms undergo long-duration variation, selection, retention, recombination, and historical reorganization across populations and generations. This arising is not a single communicative act and not one bounded symbolic object. It consists in extended trajectories of change through which vocabularies, grammatical conventions, semantic fields, ritual forms, interpretive repertoires, and transmitted cultural structures are preserved, modified, stratified, hybridized, or displaced under conditions of social transmission, institutional stabilization, conflict, prestige bias, and cross-group interaction. The arising therefore captures broad historical-cultural transformation rather than any one medium or one propagating symbolic unit, establishing a temporally extended evolutionary regime of shared meaning structures across societies.
records.name: Cultural and Linguistic Evolutionary Change
records.shortDescription: Process-level cumulative transformation of symbolic systems, languages, and transmitted cultural forms through social transmission, variation, selection, and intergenerational retention.
records.summary: Process-level cumulative transformation of symbolic systems, languages, and transmitted cultural forms through social transmission, variation, selection, and intergenerational retention.

records.description: Morphogenesis of Cities and Urban Dynamics denote the admissible pattern-level formation of large-scale socio-spatial organization in which dense and persistent settlements emerge from coupled interactions among social structure, economic exchange, governance, mobility, infrastructure, and cultural practice. This arising is not a single planning process and not one bounded institutional object, but a reproducible relational pattern distributed across territory through density gradients, transport corridors, land-use differentiation, neighborhood segregation, agglomeration structure, infrastructural layering, and feedback between built form and social function. Within SOMA this arising is classified as a pattern because its identity is determined by stable organization of spatial relations, flow structures, and heterogeneous urban subregions across many human carriers and institutions rather than by one isolated action sequence or singular governing body. Cities thereby operate as self-organizing socio-spatial systems exhibiting path dependence, uneven concentration of opportunity, infrastructural inertia, and reciprocal shaping between collective coordination and material layout. This arising establishes an autonomous urban pattern regime with its own constraints, attractors, and long-duration developmental trajectories.
records.name: Morphogenesis of Cities and Urban Dynamics
records.shortDescription: Pattern-level socio-spatial organization of dense settlements emerging from coupled social, economic, infrastructural, and regulatory interactions.
records.summary: Pattern-level socio-spatial organization of dense settlements emerging from coupled social, economic, infrastructural, and regulatory interactions.

records.description: Digital Social Networks denote the admissible pattern-level formation of large-scale socio-technical interaction graphs in which social communication, coordination, reputation management, and information exchange become persistently mediated by digital platforms and their associated ranking, recommendation, and trace-retention architectures. This arising is not a single communicative process and not one bounded platform object, but a reproducible relational pattern distributed across users, interaction histories, content traces, algorithmic curation layers, and platform-mediated feedback channels. Its identity lies in stable organization of interaction topology jointly with automated visibility management rather than in one isolated action sequence, institutional object, or social property alone. Through recommendation systems, selective amplification, trace persistence, and high-speed diffusion, these networks reshape influence distribution, collective attention, polarization dynamics, reputational accumulation, coordination thresholds, and the temporal persistence of social signals. The arising therefore formalizes a distinct socio-technical regime in which digital mediation and social structure jointly constrain large-scale collective behavior independently of any single participant's intent.
records.name: Digital Social Networks
records.shortDescription: Pattern-level socio-technical interaction graphs in which digital mediation, persistent traces, and algorithmic filtering reshape collective social dynamics at scale.
records.summary: Pattern-level socio-technical interaction graphs in which digital mediation, persistent traces, and algorithmic filtering reshape collective social dynamics at scale.

records.description: Formation of Influence Networks denotes the admissible pattern-level stabilization of asymmetric relational structures through which influence, visibility, credibility, trust, and coordination leverage become unevenly distributed across a social system. This arising is not a single persuasive event and not one bounded institutional object, but a reproducible mesoscopic pattern in which repeated interaction, reputational feedback, selective attention, mediated amplification, and differential access to audiences generate persistent who-affects-whom asymmetries. Within SOMA this arising is classified as a pattern because its identity is determined by stable organization of weighted and directed influence relations among many social carriers rather than by one isolated process, property, or formal institution. These networks channel information flow, bias opinion formation, shape agenda priority, and concentrate amplification power in specific nodes, clusters, or bridging positions across informal leadership settings, expert communities, media ecosystems, and digital platforms. The arising therefore establishes a distinct mesoscopic layer mediating between individual agency, collective cognition, and institutional authority.
records.name: Formation of Influence Networks
records.shortDescription: Pattern-level stabilization of asymmetric social graph structures that distribute influence, visibility, credibility, and coordination leverage unevenly across populations.
records.summary: Pattern-level stabilization of asymmetric social graph structures that distribute influence, visibility, credibility, and coordination leverage unevenly across populations.

records.description: Epistemic Markets and Knowledge Valuation denote the admissible process-level organization through which socially distributed systems allocate attention, credibility, interpretive weight, legitimacy, and symbolic value to informational artifacts such as claims, data, explanations, expertise, models, and conceptual frameworks. This arising consists in temporally extended processes of evaluation, endorsement, citation, ranking, reputational amplification, diffusion, contestation, recombination, and obsolescence through which informational artifacts gain or lose epistemic standing. It is not reducible to one platform or one institutional setting, but spans scientific, media, educational, policy, and digitally mediated publics in which informational selection is shaped by trust, prestige, interpretive consensus, visibility, and network effects rather than by direct exchange of physical goods. The arising therefore formalizes a distributed valuation regime that determines which ideas persist, stabilize, circulate, recombine, or decay, thereby shaping collective understanding, innovation trajectories, and epistemic stability without requiring centralized control.
records.name: Epistemic Markets and Knowledge Valuation
records.shortDescription: Process-level distributed allocation of attention, credibility, interpretive weight, and epistemic value across information and knowledge systems.
records.summary: Process-level distributed allocation of attention, credibility, interpretive weight, and epistemic value across information and knowledge systems.

records.description: Cooperation and Conflict in Large-Scale Societies denotes the admissible process-level co-organization by which mechanisms of exchange, governance, norms, identity, and information flow interact across populations that exceed the limits of direct interpersonal coordination. Within Level 7 this arising consists in temporally extended processes of alliance formation, collective goods provision, regulated competition, institutionalized rivalry, coordinated mobilization, dispute channeling, and conflict containment or escalation across large-scale social systems. Within SOMA this arising is classified as a process because its identity is defined by ongoing ordered dynamics of coordination, opposition, stabilization, and transformation unfolding through time rather than by a static social pattern, bounded institutional object, or collective property alone. Cooperation and conflict are treated here as co-evolving modes of regulation rather than simple opposites, since conflict can become structured, channeled, and institutionally organized while cooperation can depend on exclusion, competition, or rivalry boundaries. This arising shapes alliance architecture, institutional design, stability regimes, and large-scale social transformation by regulating how populations coordinate, compete, and reorganize under shared pressures.
records.name: Cooperation and Conflict in Large-Scale Societies
records.shortDescription: Process-level co-organization of large-scale cooperation and structured conflict across populations exceeding direct interpersonal coordination.
records.summary: Process-level co-organization of large-scale cooperation and structured conflict across populations exceeding direct interpersonal coordination.

records.description: Cultural Transmission, Recombination, and Idea Propagation denote the admissible pattern-level formation of socially transmitted symbolic variants that spread across individuals, institutions, media systems, and networked publics through repeated communication, imitation, reinterpretation, and selective retention. This arising is not a single communication event and not one bounded symbolic object, but a reproducible evolutionary pattern in which ideas, narratives, slogans, images, frames, and other symbolic constructs undergo branching, transformation, recombination, amplification, and extinction across time. Within SOMA this arising is classified as a pattern because its identity is determined by stable organization of transmission, variation, selection, and persistence relations among symbolic carriers rather than by one isolated process episode, institutional object, or collective property alone. These transmitted variants shape attention, belief formation, coordination, and behavior through salience, affective resonance, social prestige, network topology, and contextual fit rather than through factual accuracy alone. The arising therefore establishes a distinct cultural-evolutionary regime embedded in social systems, characterized by competitive diffusion, recurrent mutation, selective persistence, and large-scale propagation dynamics.
records.name: Cultural Transmission, Recombination, and Idea Propagation
records.shortDescription: Pattern-level propagation of socially transmitted symbolic variants that spread, mutate, recombine, and compete across populations and media.
records.summary: Pattern-level propagation of socially transmitted symbolic variants that spread, mutate, recombine, and compete across populations and media.

records.description: Social Identity and Group Belonging denotes the admissible property-level stabilization of collective affiliation structures through which in-group and out-group membership become socially and psychologically operative across populations. Within Level 7 this arising is expressed as a system-level social property in which shared norms, symbols, narratives, and feedback loops organize durable categories of belonging that individuals internalize as part of self-conception and group alignment. Within SOMA this arising is classified as a property because its identity lies in a persistent collective-affiliative condition attributable to the social system rather than in one isolated interaction process, bounded institutional object, or static network pattern alone. This arising embeds emotional, moral, and behavioral dispositions into identity structures, shaping perception, trust, cooperation, exclusion, and conflict independently of immediate incentives or explicit rules. At larger scales it amplifies internal coordination, stabilizes symbolic boundaries, and structures rivalry, alliance formation, and differentiation among groups.
records.name: Social Identity and Group Belonging
records.shortDescription: Property-level stabilization of group affiliation structures that shape loyalty, boundary formation, trust, and intergroup differentiation.
records.summary: Property-level stabilization of group affiliation structures that shape loyalty, boundary formation, trust, and intergroup differentiation.

records.description: Recurrent Social Practices denotes the admissible process-level stabilization of repeated collective action sequences within already organized social groups. Within Level 7 this arising consists in temporally extended and recurrent coordination patterns through which role-differentiated agents repeatedly enact similar configurations of cooperation, conflict resolution, signaling, resource sharing, and activity cycling. Within SOMA this arising is classified as a process because its identity is defined by ordered action sequences unfolding across time rather than by a static relational pattern, bounded object, or group-level property alone. This arising marks a transition from episodic coordination to stabilized procedural continuity, where expectations become embedded directly in repeated sequences of doing rather than in explicit rules, representations, or codified instructions. Recurrent social practices reduce uncertainty, lower coordination cost, preserve continuity across participant turnover, and enable group-level functioning to remain reliable through repeated enactment.
records.name: Recurrent Social Practices
records.shortDescription: Process-level stabilization of repeated collective action sequences within social groups, yielding durable and recognizable coordination routines.
records.summary: Process-level stabilization of repeated collective action sequences within social groups, yielding durable and recognizable coordination routines.

records.description: Societal Feedback on Individual Neurodynamics denotes the admissible effect-level cross-level influence through which stabilized social environments, from caregiving and group living to social structures, shared identities, institutions, norms, and collective affective environments, systematically bias neural activity, plasticity, stress responsivity, valuation, attentional allocation, and functional regimes within individuals. This arising is expressed as a socially induced regulatory influence in which social organization becomes neurally operative through care and contact, social evaluation, exclusion, reputational pressure, normative expectations, chronic stressors, role obligations, and institutionalized reward–penalty structures. It does not depend on one isolated interpersonal episode, but on persistent embedding of individuals within structured social environments whose patterns are repeatedly internalized through learning, affective conditioning, and state regulation. The arising therefore formalizes downward and diagonal causation from social organization to neural organization, constraining learning sensitivity, affective baseline, cognitive salience, and decision thresholds without requiring direct genetic or pharmacological intervention. Within SOMA this is an effect because its identity lies in the impact of social organization on individual neural regimes, an outcome that propagates beyond the social structure producing it into subsequent causal chains at the neural level.
records.name: Societal Feedback on Individual Neurodynamics
records.shortDescription: Effect-level downward and diagonal influence of social environments, identities, norms, and collective states on individual neural regimes.
records.summary: Effect-level downward and diagonal influence of social environments, identities, norms, and collective states on individual neural regimes.

records.description: Sociogenesis of Shared Information Environments denotes the admissible pattern-level formation of shared societal-scale informational environments produced by the integration of information flows, symbolic representations, influence networks, media infrastructures, and collective attention. This arising is not a single communication process and not one bounded media object, but a reproducible relational pattern distributed across populations through attention gradients, amplification hubs, credibility asymmetries, discourse pathways, memetic circulation, and persistent interpretive frames. Within SOMA this arising is classified as a pattern because its identity is determined by stable organization of informational relations and salience structures across many social carriers rather than by one isolated process episode, institutional object, or collective property alone. These shared information environments shape what becomes salient, discussable, credible, ignored, amplified, or suppressed across society, thereby guiding coordination, expectation, and interpretation without requiring centralized control. They function as distributed societal attractor structures with inertia, tipping points, and path dependence, modulating discourse and action across time and space.

records.shortDescription: Pattern-level formation of shared societal information environments that organize salience, credibility, interpretation, and coordination across large populations.
records.summary: Pattern-level formation of shared societal information environments that organize salience, credibility, interpretation, and coordination across large populations.

records.description: Transculturation and Hybridization of Traditions denotes the admissible pattern-level formation of hybrid cultural configurations produced through sustained interaction among distinct cultural systems. Within Level 7 this arising is not a single exchange event and not one bounded institutional object, but a reproducible large-scale pattern in which symbols, practices, narratives, identities, and interpretive forms are selectively recombined, recontextualized, and restabilized into novel cultural configurations. Within SOMA this arising is classified as a pattern because its identity is determined by stable organization of recombined cultural relations and transmission structures across populations and time rather than by one isolated process episode, collective property, or source tradition alone. This arising formalizes reciprocal transformation rather than unidirectional diffusion or simple assimilation, generating hybrid traditions that are not reducible to their cultural sources. It enables adaptation to new social, technological, and geopolitical conditions while reshaping collective memory, meaning, and identity at population scale.

records.description: Mass Cognitive Distortion Regimes denote the admissible property-level emergence of systematic collective distortion in perception, judgment, attribution, and belief formation at societal scale. This arising is expressed as a population-level epistemic condition in which individual heuristics, bounded rationality, interpretive shortcuts, and emotionally loaded salience cues become synchronized, reinforced, and amplified through social interaction, media environments, identity alignment, idea propagation, and shared information environments. It is not reducible to isolated individual error. Instead, it characterizes a stable distortion tendency attributable to the coupled social–informational–cognitive system, in which information topology, affective resonance, repeated framing, selective amplification, and group alignment jointly bias evidence evaluation, causal attribution, risk perception, and belief updating. The arising therefore formalizes how large populations can enter persistent miscalibrated interpretive regimes that shape discourse, collective behavior, and policy outcomes independently of any single individual's intent.

records.description: Global Governance and Supranational Institutions denote the admissible object-level formation of transnational coordination structures through which political authority, regulatory frameworks, collective rule-setting, monitoring, and coordinated action extend beyond individual states. This arising is treated as an object because it consists in identifiable organized formations such as treaties, multilateral organizations, international regimes, supranational bodies, and persistent transnational compliance architectures with bounded procedures, roles, decision channels, enforcement asymmetries, and coordination capacities that persist across changing participants and historical episodes. It is not merely a recurring coordination process or a diffuse global property. Rather, it forms a durable organized configuration that acquires non-sovereign yet causally effective authority across heterogeneous actors, linking states, firms, publics, and expert systems through partially institutionalized global rule structures. The arising therefore establishes a distinct global coordination object with path dependence, adaptive capacity, legitimacy conflicts, and causal influence irreducible to bilateral diplomacy or domestic governance alone.

records.description: Opinion Polarization denotes the admissible pattern-level divergence of attitudes within a population, in which social influence, identity alignment, and selective exposure move positions apart or bind them to group lines instead of drawing them toward a shared estimate. Within Level 7 this arising is not one persuasive episode and not an individual bias, but a reproducible distributional pattern of preferences, ideological positions, and affective evaluations of out-groups across many social carriers. It differs from factual miscalibration: its observable is the shape and group alignment of the attitude distribution rather than error against an external truth criterion, and exposure to opposing views can widen rather than narrow it. Within SOMA this arising is classified as a pattern because its identity is determined by the relational structure of the attitude distribution and its alignment with group boundaries rather than by one process episode, bounded object, or property of single individuals. Polarized distributions constrain deliberation, cooperation, and conflict between groups, and they persist through identity-consistent selection of information and partners.

records.shortDescription: Pattern-level divergence and group-aligned sorting of attitudes in a population under social influence and identity alignment.
records.summary: Pattern-level divergence and group-aligned sorting of attitudes in a population under social influence and identity alignment.

records.description: Social Exchange and Resource Coordination denotes the admissible process-level stabilization of regulated mechanisms for distributing, transferring, and managing shared resources within organized social groups. Within Level 7 this arising consists in temporally extended exchange and allocation sequences such as reciprocal transfer, redistribution, obligation-based delivery, queueing, priority access, and coordinated management of common goods. Within SOMA this arising is classified as a process because its identity is defined by ordered flows of material, energetic, and access-related transfers unfolding through time rather than by one static relational pattern, bounded object, or intrinsic property. This arising marks a transition from situational cooperation to regulated resource flow, where exchanges are increasingly shaped by collective arrangements, persistent expectations, and group-level coordination structures rather than by immediate bilateral interaction alone. It enables scalability, temporal persistence, conflict reduction, buffering against local scarcity, and more stable collective metabolism within social systems.

records.summary: Process-level stabilization of regulated exchange, allocation, and coordinated resource flow within social groups.

records.description: Collective Decision-Making denotes the admissible process-level organization by which socially organized groups aggregate distributed signals, preferences, constraints, or action tendencies into a single group-level outcome. Within Level 7 this arising consists in temporally extended mechanisms such as consensus formation, quorum dynamics, majority convergence, leader-mediated selection, and distributed decision cascades through which multiple local inputs are transformed into one stabilized collective choice. Within SOMA this arising is classified as a process because its identity is defined by ordered aggregation, convergence, threshold transition, and outcome stabilization unfolding through time rather than by a static group pattern, bounded object, or intrinsic property. The resulting decision is not attributable to any single individual but is produced by interaction topology, information flow, asymmetries of influence, and coordination procedures embedded in the group. This arising establishes a causal regime in which group-level choice reorganizes subsequent individual behavior, future coordination pathways, and shared collective action.

records.description: Structures of Human Society denotes the admissible pattern-level stabilization of persistent large-scale social organization extending beyond immediate face-to-face groups. Within Level 7 this arising is not a single coordinated process and not one bounded collective object, but a reproducible relational pattern spanning populations through stratified layers, kinship and descent arrangements, territorial ordering, authority distributions, and durable frameworks of coordination maintained across generations. Within SOMA this arising is classified as a pattern because its identity is determined by stable organization of relations among many human carriers and subgroups rather than by one isolated action sequence, institution, or intrinsic property. This arising functions as an abstract social ordering principle that constrains individual and group behavior independently of specific participants, enabling continuity, scalability, institutional persistence, intergenerational transmission, and cumulative social complexity. It marks the stabilization of society-level structure as a distinct organizational regime beyond local interaction networks.

records.shortDescription: Pattern-level persistent large-scale social organization structuring human populations beyond immediate groups through durable positional and coordinative arrangements.
records.summary: Pattern-level persistent large-scale social organization structuring human populations beyond immediate groups through durable positional and coordinative arrangements.

records.description: Collective Intelligence under Distributed Aggregation denotes the admissible property-level cognitive capacity of socially structured populations to transform distributed individual signals into reliable group-level judgments, solutions, forecasts, or problem-solving outcomes when diversity of perspective, partial independence, structured aggregation, and network-level coordination jointly support improved inference under uncertainty. This arising is not identical to one voting rule or one communication format. It consists in a stable capacity attributable to the organized collective when error cancellation, distributed exploration of solution spaces, selective signal integration, confidence-weighting, redundancy reduction, and aggregation architecture together allow the group as a whole to infer, estimate, or solve more effectively than typical isolated participants. Wisdom-of-crowds effects form one important special case of this broader capacity, but the arising also includes more interactive forms of collective problem solving in which coordination, role differentiation, and iterative exchange alter group-level epistemic performance. Within SOMA this is classified as a property because its identity lies in a capability attributable to the organized collective system rather than in one isolated decision process, bounded institutional object, or static interaction pattern alone.

records.summary: Property-level group cognitive capacity in which distributed populations integrate partially independent contributions into judgments or solutions that can outperform typical individual performance under suitable aggregation conditions.

records.description: Superorganism Behavior in Insect Colonies denotes the admissible process-level organization in which large populations of relatively simple insects coordinate through local interactions to generate coherent adaptive behavior at the colony level. Within Level 7 this arising consists in temporally extended colony-wide processes such as foraging, nest construction, brood care, defense, reproduction, environmental regulation, and dynamic task reallocation under changing internal and external conditions. Within SOMA this arising is classified as a process because its identity is defined by ordered and ongoing colony-level behavioral coordination unfolding through time rather than by a static relational pattern, bounded collective object, or global property alone. The colony thereby functions as an integrated higher-order behavioral unit in which caste differentiation, pheromonal signaling, contact-based interactions, feedback-regulated task allocation, and homeostatic adjustment jointly sustain adaptive collective performance. This arising persists independently of individual identities and is irreducible to single-organism control, establishing colony-level behavior as a distinct organizational regime.

records.description: Social Norms and Conventions denotes the admissible property-level emergence of shared expectation structures that regulate behavior within socially organized groups. Within Level 7 this arising is expressed as a system-level regulatory condition in which appropriate and inappropriate behavior become collectively anticipated through recurrent interaction, mutual monitoring, reputation effects, approval, disapproval, and exclusion dynamics. Within SOMA this arising is classified as a property because its identity lies in a persistent regulatory condition attributable to the social system rather than in one isolated action sequence, bounded collective object, or static positional pattern. These norms and conventions operate without centralized enforcement, embedding behavioral constraints directly into the expectation architecture of the group and thereby reducing coordination costs, stabilizing interaction under uncertainty, and enabling cooperation across larger social scales. This arising formalizes informal social regulation as a distinct collective property of the system.

records.description: Dynamics of Economic Markets denotes the admissible process-level emergence of decentralized price formation, allocation, and coordination of production and consumption through large-scale social exchange. Within Level 7 this arising consists in temporally extended transactional and informational processes through which distributed local decisions aggregate into global patterns such as prices, volumes, volatility, cycles, shortages, surpluses, bubbles, and crashes. Within SOMA this arising is classified as a process because its identity is defined by ongoing ordered exchanges, adjustments, feedback loops, and regime transitions unfolding through time rather than by a static institutional pattern, bounded collective object, or single system property. This arising constitutes a social regulatory regime that coordinates resources without centralized control, relying on distributed interaction, expectation formation, signal propagation, trust structures, and adaptive response to changing conditions. It exhibits nonlinearity, path dependence, episodic instability, and emergent large-scale coordination irreducible to isolated individual decisions.
